title: A Deep Learning Approach for Spatial Multi-omics Cell Clustering
role: Lead Student Researcher (Final Year Design Project)
tagline: Unsupervised representation learning for multi-modal biological data and cellular niche identification
summary: Focuses on applying deep learning architectures to spatial multi-omics data to decipher complex cellular microenvironments. By bridging artificial intelligence and computational biology, this work explores how multi-modal biological data can be integrated into low-dimensional latent representations for accurate, unsupervised cell clustering and spatial domain identification.
researchQuestions: How can diverse biological modalities (e.g., spatial transcriptomics and proteomics) be effectively fused without losing spatial context?
Can deep unsupervised representation learning disentangle batch effects while preserving biologically meaningful cellular heterogeneity?
How can learned spatial embeddings improve the identification of rare cellular niches and tissue architectural boundaries?
methodology: Multi-modal biological data preprocessing, normalization, and quality control.
Designing deep latent representation learning frameworks (Autoencoders / Graph Neural Networks) that capture spatial coordinate topologies alongside molecular abundance.
Unsupervised clustering algorithms evaluated across benchmark spatial multi-omics datasets.
Biological validation via marker gene expression analysis and spatial domain consistency.
